stem: Which one of the following statements best describes the standard deviation?
options: It is a measure of how close the sample mean is to the population mean
It is a measure of the spread of the sample distribution relative to the mean
It is derived from the difference between the mean and the median
It is derived from the p value
Its numerical value is 1.96
explanation:
It is a measure of the spread of the sample distribution relative to the mean
It is derived from the square root of the variance. A higher standard deviation (SD) represents a greater spread of values.

It is a measure of how close the sample mean is to the population mean
It is a measure of how close the sample mean is to the population mean is incorrect. This is in fact describing the standard error of the mean.

It is derived from the difference between the mean and the median
It is derived from the difference between the mean and the median is incorrect. The SD is derived from the square root of the variance.

It is derived from the p value
It is derived from the p value is incorrect. The SD is not directly related to the p value. The pChat valuewith is used to determine the statistical significance of the findings and the SD is not derived from this.

stem: A study is being planned to investigate any link between environmental exposure to pesticides and cases of cancer. Which one of the following study designs is most appropriate?
options: Case-control study
Case series
Cohort study
Cross-sectional survey
Randomised controlled trial
explanation:
Case-control study
In a case-control study, the past history of pesticide exposure in a group of patients with cancer (cases) would be compared with that of a group of patients without cancer (controls). This would enable us to answer the study question and also avoids the need for the long and expensive follow-up required for a cohort study.

Case series
Case series is incorrect. A case series would consist of a number of patients with cancer who have a past history of exposure to pesticides. While this may be suggestive of a link, it is a very low level of evidence and so, not the most appropriate study design.

Cross-sectional survey
Cross-sectional survey is incorrect. A cross-sectional study is a “snapshot” study at a specified time with no longitudinal follow-up. It would provide us with the prevalence of cancer, but not the incidence.

stem: A cross-sectional study examining population characteristics in a small UK town finds that blood pressure and age are normally distributed. What statistic best describes the accuracy with which the UK population mean can be estimated?
options: Coefficient of variation
Skewness
Standard deviation
Standard error
Variance
explanation:
Standard error
The standard error (or standard error of the mean) is a measure of how precisely the sample mean approximates the population mean.

Coefficient of variation
Coefficient of variation is incorrect. The coefficient of variation (the standard deviation divided by the mean) is an appropriate measure for distributions where all values are positive, so it would not be appropriate in a normal distribution.

Skewness
Skewness is incorrect. Skewness describes how asymmetrical a distribution is and does not really concern the mean.

stem: A new test is developed for the diagnosis of hepatitis C. Out of 10,000 tests 100 were positive using the current gold standard method (assumed to be 100% accurate) for diagnosing hepatitis C, whereas using the new method 150 tests were positive, (100 from the original cohort, and a further 50). What is the positive predictive value of the new test?
explanation:
66%
We know from the gold standard test that the number of true positives is 100. We also know from the new test that it has generated 150 positive results. 50 of these must therefore actually be false positives. The positive predictive value (PPV) of a test = true positive ÷ (true positive + false positive) = 100 ÷ (100 + 50).

50%
50% is incorrect. You may have erroneously obtained 50 from 150 positive new method tests minus 100 positive gold standard tests or by thinking there were 50% more positive tests using the new methods compared to the gold standard. Either way, both of these rationale are incorrect. The PPV is calculated using the formula above.

stem: A study is planned into the effects on risk of myocardial infarction of a new lipid modifying agent, and the steering committee states that they plan to include number needed to treat (NNT) as part of the primary manuscript. How is the number needed to treat over the duration of the study calculated?
options: Number of months of study divided by the absolute risk reduction
Ratio of absolute to relative risk reduction
Ratio of relative to absolute risk reduction
Reciprocal of absolute risk reduction
Reciprocal of relative risk reduction
explanation:
Reciprocal of absolute risk reduction
The NNT can be calculated by 1/ARR. For the remainder of the question, it is helpful to have a working example. We will use a previous question to work out the answers. A study in patients aged 75 and over measures the effectiveness of warfarin versus aspirin with regards to reduction of embolic stroke over a 10 month period. After the study has closed the group treated with warfarin has a 1.2% risk of embolic stroke over the period of the trial, whereas those on aspirin have a 2.4% risk. The absolute risk reduction (ARR) = standard treatment events (aspirin) – new treatment events (warfarin) = 2.4% – 1.2% = 1.2%. NNT = 1 / ARR = 1/0.012 = 83.3333.

stem: A study measuring disease spread in a population is being conducted. Each member of the population has an independent probability of 25% of carrying the disease. A random sample of 12 people is taken to study. What is the distribution of the number of people carrying the disease in the random sample of 12 people drawn from this population?
options: Binomial with n = 12, p = 0.25
Chi-squared with 3 degrees of freedom
Normal with mean = 3, standard deviation = 1.5
Poisson with lambda = 3
Uniform with p = 1/12
explanation:
Binomial with n = 12, p = 0.25
A binomial distribution described the number of times an event occurs from a fixed number of opportunities when the probability that the event occurs at each opportunity is constant and independent. The distribution is characterised by the number of opportunities (n) and the probability of an event (p). In this question, the sample size is 12 people (or 12 opportunities for the disease to occur), so n=12. The probability is given as 25%, or p=0.25 as a decimal.

Normal with mean = 3, standard deviation = 1.5
Normal with mean = 3, standard deviation = 1.5 is incorrect. A normal distribution would be an inappropriate answer to this question, which concerns probability.

stem: A study of patients receiving peritoneal dialysis (PD) as renal replacement therapy is carried out to test the hypothesis that an increasing number of episodes of PD-associated peritonitis is associated with decreased time to failure of the peritoneal membrane. Which one of the following procedures is appropriate for analysing the results?
options: F-test
Kruskal–Wallis test
One-sample t-test
One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA)
Spearman’s rank correlation
explanation:
Spearman’s rank correlation
Spearman’s rank correlation tests for an association between the number of episodes of PD peritonitis and the rank order of the failure times. This is the most appropriate statistical test for analysing this dataset.

F-test
F-test is incorrect. The F-test compares the variances of two independent samples. Samples in this test are dependent as they are compared within patients.

One-sample t-test
One-sample t-test is incorrect. The one-sample t-test compares the mean of a sample to a prespecified value, and as such, is inappropriate in this dataset.

stem: Which one of the following statements concerning the distribution curve is accurate?
options: In any given distribution there is only one mode
The mean is a good measure of central tendency in skewed distributions
The mean value is lower than the median in positively skewed distributions
The median is the sum of all the scores divided by the number of scores
When there is an even number of numbers, the median is the mean of the two middle numbers
explanation:
When there is an even number of numbers, the median is the mean of the two middle numbers
The median is the central number in a distribution once you have placed all values in a dataset in order of their value. As the statement explains, if there are an even number of values, the two middle numbers are added together and then then divided by two to obtain the median. The median is less sensitive to extreme scores than the mean and this makes it a better measure than the mean for highly skewed distributions.

In any given distribution there is only one mode
In any given distribution there is only one mode is incorrect. The mode is the value that occurs with the highest frequency. However, there is the possibility that two or more values have the same frequency but also have the highest frequency within a dataset. For example, in a sample 100 students and their exam scores, 10AIstudents Tutor achieved 71%, 10 students achieved 73% and 10 students achieved 74%. No other score had a higher frequency meaning the modes are 71%, 73% & 74%, i.e. more than one value.

The median is the sum of all the scores divided by the number of scores
The median is the sum of all the scores divided by the number of scores is incorrect. This is actually describing the mean. The median is the central number in a distribution once you have placed all values in a dataset in order of their value.

stem: An observational study of immunoglobulin G (IgG) levels was carried in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)- and non-HIV-infected individuals. The two large groups studied were similar with respect to age and sex; there are no other potential confounding factors that need to be corrected for. The IgG levels recorded had a positively skewed distribution. What statistical significance test is best for comparing the average IgG levels of the two groups?
options: Multiple regression analysis
The Chi-square test (contingency table analysis)
The Mann–Whitney U-test
The Spearman correlation coefficient
The Student unpaired t-test
explanation:
The Mann–Whitney U-test
Working through this question, note that IgG levels had a positively skewed distribution. This means that this is not a normal distribution, so we will need to use non-parametric testing in order to compare groups. This rules out the Student’s t-test immediately. As we are comparing averages in non-parametric distribution, the best method would be to use the Mann-Whitney U-test.

The Spearman correlation coefficient
The Spearman correlation coefficient is incorrect. As the groups studied were similar in terms of age and sex (potential confounders), correlation analysis is not required.

stem: In the design of a randomised controlled trial studying the effects of metformin + repaglinide compared to metformin monotherapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, to what does the ‘power of the study’ refer?
options: The chance that a clinically significant difference will be observed
The probability of a statistically significant treatment effect if the true treatment difference is at a
The probability of a type-2 error
The probability of rejecting the null hypothesis that the treatments have the same effect
The size of treatment difference that the trial can be expected to detect
explanation:
The probability of a statistically significant treatment effect if the true treatment difference is at a
prespecified level The hypothesis of a randomised controlled trial is usually that there will be a difference between treatment and control groups. Therefore, the null hypothesis will be that there is no difference between treatment and control groups. The power of a study is the probability (which is usually expressed as a percentage) of correctly rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false. Therefore, Option B is the best answer as it correctly fulfills the criteria describing power, as well as stating that the difference is at a prespecified level.

The probability of a type-2 error
The probability of a type-2 error is incorrect. This is the opposite of power. A type II error occurs when the null hypothesis is false, which gives a high p-value.

stem: In a parallel group trial studying the effects of either ramipril or losartan on proteinuria in chronic kidney disease, which one of the following claims for randomisation is the most appropriate?
options: Any differences in response found between the treatment groups must be due to the treatments
It ensures that an equal number of patients receive each treatment
It guarantees that all variables are well balanced across the treatment groups prior to treatment
It prevents systematic differences in specified variables between the treatment groups at baseline
It results in a simplified analysis of the trial
explanation:
It prevents systematic differences in specified variables between the treatment groups at baseline
Randomisation constitutes the allocation of individuals to groups (for example, into study and control groups), by chance. Randomisation follows a predetermined plan that usually employs a random number table. Within the limits of chance variation, randomisation should achieve similarity between the study and control groups at baseline. It should also ensure that personal judgment and prejudices of an investigator do not influence group allocation. As the purpose of randomisation to prevent systematic differences between study groups, this option is the best choice.

Any differences in response found between the treatment groups must be due to the treatments
rather than chance

It guarantees that all variables are well balanced across the treatment groups prior to treatment
It guarantees that all variables are well balanced across the treatment groups prior to treatment is incorrect. Randomisation does not guarantee equal balance of variables across treatment groups (because it’s random!).

stem: You are working on a submission to the local formulary committee about new treatment for heart failure. The formulary committee wishes to see data about the impact on costs of heart failure within the locality of instituting the new treatment. Which of the following would provide the most useful evidence?
options: Healthcare utilisation study vs standard of care
Modelled data on events based on the phase 3 study
Observational analysis of heart failure admissions
Phase 3 data vs placebo
US claims data published after the launch of the product
explanation:
Healthcare utilisation study vs standard of care
Cost effectiveness can be different from clinical effectiveness, although the two are of course interlinked. The gold standard for healthcare utilisation data is a specific study, including measurement of time spent in hospital, contact with GP services, and the cost of any interventions.

Observational analysis of heart failure admissions
Observational analysis of heart failure admissions is incorrect. Observational analysis can be used to see if there is a link but would not be a robust enough study in its own right. Further studies would need to be carried out to support the initial findings.

stem: In a prospective clinical trial, 140 patients with hepatitis were randomly allocated to receive either a new drug or conventional treatment; the patients were followed up for between 3 and 5 years. When evaluating the study results, a Chi-square test can be used to compare the two groups with respect to:
options: Mean survival times
Median survival times
The proportions of patients who died within five years of starting their treatment
The proportions of patients who died within three years of starting their treatment
The proportions of patients who had died when the study was terminated
explanation:
The proportions of patients who died within three years of starting their treatment
A chi-squared test is any statistical test based on the comparison of a test statistic to a chi-squared distribution. The oldest and most common chi-squared tests are for determining whether two or more population distributions differ from one another. These tests usually involve counts of data and may involve comparison of samples from the distributions under study, or the comparison of a sample to a theoretically expected distribution. In simpler terms, a chi-squared test is used to compare proportion between two groups and can only be used to compare categorical measures. Measures are only comparable at a fixed timepoint and all subjects must have been followed up for the same amount of time. Therefore, in terms of the question, we are looking at an answer where proportions are compared, leaving only the proportions of patients who died within five years of starting their treatment, the proportions of patients who died within three years of starting their treatment and the proportions of patients who had died when the study was terminated. However, because a range is given for follow-up in the study, we must pick the option at the lowest timepoint of the range, because this is the last possible point at which all patients willwith Chat have the same follow-up.

stem: A consecutive series of 100 patients presenting to the emergency department with abdominal pain were studied. Thirty-five patients were eventually diagnosed as having acute appendicitis, of whom 21 had a temperature greater than 37.5 °C on admission. Twenty-nine of the patients who did not have appendicitis also had a temperature above 37.5 °C on admission. The positive predictive value of a raised temperature as a screen for appendicitis in patients presenting to this emergency department with abdominal pain is?
explanation:
42%
Let’s draw up a contingency table for this question: Diagnosis Temperature on admission Total Acute appendicitis Other >37.5C 21 29 50 =<37.5C 14 36 50 Total 35 65 100 Therefore, as the positive predictive value is the proportion of those testing positive who actually have the disease.The specificity is the proportion of true negatives correctly identified by the test.The sensitivity is the proportion of true positives correctly identified by the test.

stem: Which one of the following groups is arranged as nominal scale data?
options: Hot/cold
Hot/hotter/hottest
None
explanation:
Hot/cold
Nominal data is divided into qualitative groups that are mutually exclusive with no implication of an order.

81–90/91–100/101–110 °C
81–90/91–100/101–110 °C is incorrect. This is describing interval data. Here the data is placed in some form of an order. The exact measurements are given, usually in measured quantities representing the difference between two measurements (81–90/91–100/101–110 °C). This means differences between arbitrary pairs of measurements can be directly compared.

271–280/281–290/291–300 kelvin
271–280/281–290/291–300 kelvin is incorrect. This is describing ratio data. Ratio data has the same properties as interval data but, in addition to this, also have a clear definition of O. So with ratio data, if the variable = 0, then there is none of this variable. Temperature expressed as Fahrenheit or Celsius is not a ratio variable as 2 Celsius is not half of 4 Celsius. However, Kelvin is a ratio variable as O Kelvin means ‘no heat’. Weight can also be a ratio variable a 4 grams is double 2 grams.

stem: Which is the most characteristic feature of an ogive?
options: The first decile is equal to the 90th percentile and has 10% of the observations in the ordered set
The first percentile has 99% of the observations in the ordered set below it
The interquartile range lies between the first and third quartiles
The mean is equal to the 50th percentile
The range is the difference between the 1st and 99th percentiles
explanation:
The interquartile range lies between the first and third quartiles
The interquartile range lies between 25%-75% which is the equivalent of first and third quartiles meaning this statement is correct.  An ogive is a continuous cumulative frequency curve whereby the central point has 50% of values above it and 50% below it.

stem: The table of results shown below is for an antibody test for coeliac disease. Subjects underwent the antibody test and the presence of disease was then confirmed with small bowel biopsy. Antibody test result: Positive Negative Coeliac disease 40 10 No coeliac disease 60 890 What is the positive predictive value of the test?
explanation:
40%
The positive predictive value equals true positives / (true positives + false positives), or 40 / (40+60) = 40%. The negative predictive value equals true negatives / (true negatives + false negatives), or 890/ (890+10) = 99%. In the case of an antibody test for coeliac, a high positive predictive value or precision is needed, as the objective is to have a non-invasive test approximating to endoscopy findings, avoiding the need to proceed to the invasive test. This test is therefore not particularly useful. The sensitivity (TP/(TP+FN)) of the test is 40 / (40+10) = 80% and the specificity TN/(TN+FP) is 890 / (890+60) = 94%.

stem: The data taken from a recent local audit into results of initial CT pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) and diagnosis of pulmonary embolism for 600 ward patients is detailed below: Present Absent Total CTPA Positive Result 70 20 90 CTPA Negative Result 30 480 510 Total 100 500 600 What is the likelihood of a positive test result indicating the presence of a pulmonary embolism?
explanation:
78%
The likelihood of a positive test which indicates presents of a pulmonary embolism can also be referred to as the positive predictive value (PPV). Therefore this question asks to calculate the positive predictive value. Therefore the number of true positives/total number of positive results = 70/90 = 78%.

94%
94% is incorrect. This represents the negative predictive value i.e. the number of true negatives divided by the total number of negative results = 480/510 = 94%.

stem: You are performing a meta-analysis of the effect of ACE inhibition on major adverse cardiovascular endpoints and are determining the best way to represent the data. Which of the following is the best form for graphically representing the data?
options: Forest plot
Histogram
Pie chart
Scatter plot
Venn diagram
explanation:
Forest plot
A forest plot is also known as a blobbogram and is a graphical display that shows the relative strength of treatment effects in multiple studies addressing the same question. It was developed for use as the best means of graphically representing a meta-analysis of the results of randomized controlled trials.

Histogram
Histogram is incorrect. Histograms (also known as bar charts) are useful for looking at frequencies. The size of the box is proportional to the number within that group. This form of graph would not be able to adequately show the results of the meta-analysis.

Scatter plot
Scatter plot is incorrect. Scatter plots are best for demonstrating the relationship between two variables, e.g. blood pressure and age, or weight and age.

stem: Twenty-three consecutive adult patients attending a Dermatology Outpatients Clinic with atopic dermatitis are assessed with the six area, six sign, atopic dermatitis (SASSAD) score. The mean SASSAD score is found to be 28 with a 95% confidence interval of 26.5 to 29.5. Which one of the following statements best describes the interpretation of the 95% confidence interval?
options: 95% of patients in this population have an SASSAD score between 26.5 and 29.5
95% of the entire UK adult population will have an SASSAD score between 26.5 and 29.5
95% of the patients in the sample of 23 had an SASSAD score between 26.5 and 29.5
We are 95% confident that the mean SASSAD score in the UK adult population is between 26.5 and
We are 95% confident that the mean SASSAD score in this population is between 26.5 and 29.5
explanation:
We are 95% confident that the mean SASSAD score in this population is between 26.5 and 29.5
The 95% confidence interval for the mean is an interval that has a 95% chance of containing the true value of the mean for a particular population. The 95% confidence interval tells us about the precision with which we can estimate the mean, and not about the distribution of individual values in the sample. This option correctly describes the properties of the 95% confidence interval for the mean in the population in the question.

95% of the patients in the sample of 23 had an SASSAD score between 26.5 and 29.5
95% of the patients in the sample of 23 had an SASSAD score between 26.5 and 29.5 is incorrect. This misinterprets the 95% confidence interval – it is the probability that the given range contains the true mean not the range in which 95% of the population have their SASSAD score.

stem: You are assessing the results of a part 1 MRCP course and decide that you will examine pre- and post-test scores of each candidate to decide if the improvement is statistically significant or not. Which of the following tests is the most appropriate to test for a statistically significant improvement in test scores?
options: Two-tailed paired t-test
Two-tailed unpaired t-test
Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient
ANCOVA
Mann-Witney U test
explanation:
Two-tailed paired t-test
This is because we are interested in the change seen in pairs of results from the same individuals, before and after the course. It needs to be two-tailed because you cannot exclude the possibility that scores may actually have deteriorated as a result of the training. It is used to define the relationship between two variables, for example, weight and blood pressure or in this case pre- and post-course test scores.

Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient
Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient (SPCC) in incorrect. SPCC measures correlation between two data sets so you would be looking at correlation between the groups rather than difference in before and after scores.

stem: A regional hospital are deciding whether to introduce a new higher sensitivity troponin to their laboratories to ensure less myocardial infarctions are missed (reducing the threshold of diagnosis) and clinical diagnosis is made sooner. Through introduction of this new higher sensitivity troponin, which of the following is the most likely impact?
options: Decreased sensitivity
Increased false negative rate
Increased negative predictive value
Increased positive predictive value
Increased specificity
explanation:
Increased negative predictive value
The chance that a normal test is a true negative will occur with the introduction of the new test. Altering the diagnostic threshold of an investigation will influence the sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value and the positive predictive value. In this example, by increasing the number of patients diagnosed with myocardial infarction, the sensitivity of the test is increased (i.e. the ability of the test to detect those who truly have this disease) and therefore the negative predictive value is increased since the number of false negatives of decreased.

Increased positive predictive value
Increased positive predictive value is incorrect. The specificity of the test is inversely proportional to the sensitivity. Therefore by reducing the threshold of the test to increase the number of diagnoses, this increases the sensitivity and subsequently decreases the specificity (the ability of the test to detect those without disease). Therefore if the specificity is decreased, the positive predictive value (PPV) of the test is also decreased, as PPV represents the ability of the test to distinguish the true positives from all the positive results.

stem: You are investigating the association of a gene polymorphism with the development of obesity. You suspect that the gene may not specifically cause obesity, but make it more likely for patients to gain weight. Which one of the following statistical analyses is likely to be most meaningful with respect to expressing the association?
options: Chi squared testing
Odds ratio
Mantel-Cox
Student’s t-test
Mantel-Haenszel
explanation:
Odds ratio
The association of gene polymorphisms and specific diseases is usually expressed as an odds ratio. This is of particular value when the functionality of a particular gene isn’t identified and a range of targets are explored for a specific disease.

Chi squared testing
Chi squared testing is incorrect. Chi squared testing is used to assess if recorded observations fit a particular model.

Mantel-Cox
Mantel-Cox is incorrect. It looks at differences between the survival distributions for two populations and is therefore not appropriate in this situation.

stem: Clinically obese patients are randomised to receive either intensive dietician follow-up or normal treatment. You are provided with data on mean weight change, rather than data on weight at the beginning and end of the trial. Which one of the following tests is appropriate to test whether the mean weight loss is different between the two groups?
options: Analysis of variance (ANOVA)
F-test
Independent samples t-test
Paired samples t-test
Z-test
explanation:
Independent samples t-test
An independent (or unpaired) samples t-test compares the means in two unrelated groups, which would be the statistical test of choice in this question.

Analysis of variance (ANOVA)
Analysis of variance (ANOVA) is incorrect. ANOVA compares means across multiple groups (not just two groups), so would be inappropriate for analysis in this trial.

F-test
F-test is incorrect. An F-test is used to compare the variance of two groups, which is not what we are looking for in this question.

stem: In a small double-blind study of pain following dental surgery, patients are randomly allocated to receive either an analgesic tablet or a matching placebo tablet 1 hour preoperatively. All patients were asked to rate their pain at 4 hours after surgery using the following scale: 0 = nil, 1 = mild, 2 = moderate, 3 = severe. What is the best statistical test for analysing the results of this study?
options: Chi-square test
Fisher exact test
Mann–Whitney U-test
One-way analysis of variance
Unpaired Student t-test
explanation:
Mann–Whitney U-test
This is a double-blind randomised controlled trial where the primary outcome is given on an ordinal scale. The Mann-Whitney U-test is used for non-parametric data, which would be the most likely distribution in an randomised control trial (RCT). It compares two populations of ordinal scales, so it would be the best option of the five given for analysing the above trial.

One-way analysis of variance
One-way analysis of variance is incorrect. One-way analysis of variance (also called ANOVA) is a statistical technique that isolates and assesses the contribution of categorical independent variables to variation in the mean of a continuous dependent variable. Here, we are neither analysing against a continuous variable or a dependent variable (we are comparing proportions between two groups).

stem: In a distribution skewed by the presence of a number of positive outliers, which of the following is correct?
options: Mean increases, median increases, mode increases
Mean increases, median may increase, mode usually remains the same
Mean increases, median remains the same, mode increases
Mean remains the same, median remains the same, mode increases
Mean remains the same, median remains the same, mode remains the same
explanation:
Mean increases, median may increase, mode usually remains the same
A normal distribution is one of the most common statistical distributions. It is symmetrical and bell-shaped, with all the measures of centre equal i.e. mode=mean=median. This property is not seen in a skewed distribution. A positively skewed distribution (tail on the right) the mean is greater than the median and greater than the mode. This is because the mean is the measure of central tendency most sensitive to extreme scores and increased by the addition of large values. The mode is uninfluenced by the small number of extreme values as it only indicates the value that occurs most frequently in the distribution. The opposite would occur in a negative distribution.

Mean remains the same, median remains the same, mode remains the same
Mean remains the same, median remains the same, mode remains the same is incorrect. With positively skewed distributions, the mean will increase being greater than the median and mode. The median may also increase but to a lesser extent than the mean.

stem: A study measures the reduction in Hb A 1c in patients with type-2 diabetes randomised to receive either a new drug or standard therapy. Which one of the following tests is most appropriate to test the hypothesis that the mean Hb A 1c reduction is different in the two groups?
options: Mann–Whitney U-test
McNemar’s test
Paired t-test
Unpaired t-test
Wilcoxon signed-rank test
explanation:
Unpaired t-test
The ideal statistical method to compare means in two independent (unrelated) groups is an unpaired t-test.

Mann–Whitney U-test
Mann–Whitney U-test is incorrect. The Mann–Whitney U-test is a non-parametric test and compares the overall distributions between groups, rather than the mean values.

McNemar’s test
McNemar’s test is incorrect. McNemar’s test is used to compare proportions, rather than means.

stem: A study is undertaken to investigate the impact of simple hygiene measures on the rates of MRSA contamination of doctors’ tourniquets. A random sample of tourniquets is swabbed before the intervention, and a second random sample is tested after the intervention. The results are presented in a 2×2 contingency table, and the reduction in MRSA contamination rates is tested with a Chi-squared test. The result of the Chi-squared test is reported as ‘χ 2 = 4.8, p = 0.03’. What does ‘p = 0.03’ mean?
options: 3% of doctors’ tourniquets are contaminated with MRSA
If the experiment were to be repeated 100 times, this result would be found at least 3 times
The probability that a difference of this magnitude would have occurred by chance is 3%
The probability that this intervention has reduced the contamination rate is 3%
The rate of contamination has been reduced by 3%
explanation:
The probability that a difference of this magnitude would have occurred by chance is 3%
In a chi-squared test, the p-value refers to the probability that a result of equal or greater magnitude to the actual result of the study would have occurred by chance if the intervention had no effect, i.e. if the null hypothesis is true. Therefore, in this case, the p-value represents a 3% probability of the difference occurring by chance.

The probability that this intervention has reduced the contamination rate is 3%
The probability that this intervention has reduced the contamination rate is 3% is incorrect. It misinterprets the p-value as the reduction rate in infection.

stem: The blood pressures of a random sample of 30-year-old male civil servants are measured as part of a study into hypertension and stress. From this sample the average blood pressure in the population of 30-year-old civil servants is estimated. The precision of this estimate will depend on which one of the following?
options: Mean and sample size
Mean and standard deviation
Median and mean
Standard deviation and sample size
Variability of stress scores and sample size
explanation:
Standard deviation and sample size
Precision is a description of random errors, measure of statistical variability and is often used to describe the repeatability and reproducibility of a test. That is will repeated observations under the same conditions produce the same results. This is most closely related to the standard error which is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of statistic. The sample size is also key when discussing precision. With smaller sample sizes we see larger ranges and larger samples lead to smaller ranges and therefore more precision.

Mean and standard deviation
Mean and standard deviation is incorrect. The mean gives you a snapshot view of a data set but does not influence the precision. It is the sum of all the values in a given dataset divided by the total number of values you added up. Precision is most closely related to the standard deviation/error.

stem: You are drawing up a trial of a new screening test. Initially the test results show that 45 people have a negative test and do not have the disease. However, once the test is adjusted and finalised it shows that 55 people from the same sample do not have the disease and have a negative test. In this scenario, which one of the following is being described as increasing?
options: Incidence
Positive predictive value
Prevalence
Sensitivity
Specificity
explanation:
Specificity
The specificity of a test is the ability of a test to correctly identify those that do not have the disease. As the number of people correctly picked up as not having the disease by the test has increased, it must be the specificity that has increased.

Incidence
Incidence is incorrect. The incidence is the risk of contracting the disease so remains independent of the test and therefore will be unaffected by changes to the test.

Prevalence
Prevalence is incorrect. The prevalence describes how widespread the disease is. Again, this is independent of the test and therefore will be unaffected by changes to the test.

stem: Regarding definitions of true- and false-positive and -negative rates, which of the following is true?

The false-positive rate is calculated as (false-positive/[true-positive + false-positive])
The true-negative rate is (1 – false-negative rate)

explanation:

The sensitivity looks at correctly identifying those with the disease and the false-negative rate looks at those with the disease that test negatively. Both the sensitivity and false-negative rate look at people with the disease. If we say, the sensitivity is 90% the true-positive would be 9 and the false-negative would be 1. False-negative rate = 1-sensitivity = 1-0.9 =0.1=10%=1 person.

A perfect test would have a sensitivity of at least 70%
A perfect test would have a sensitivity of at least 70% is incorrect. Sensitivity looks at the ability of a test to correctly identify those with the disease. The perfect test would correctly identify everyone and would have a sensitivity of 100%

The false-positive rate is calculated as (false-positive/[true-positive + false-positive]) is incorrect.The false- positive rate relates to people without the disease that test positive meaning, it is related to specificity and the true-negative rate.

stem: You are examining data from a study on the comparison of a new agent for the treatment of neuropathic pain versus tricyclic anti-depressants and opiate analgesics. Data on pain has been recorded using a visual analogue scale on a number of occasions over 6 months. Which of the following is the most appropriate choice for statistical analysis in this situation?

Kruskall Wallis ANOVA
Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient
Student’s T-test
explanation:
Kruskall Wallis ANOVA
Thw Kruskall Wallis ANOVA is the most appropriate statistical test here. It is the ANOVA method of choice for non-parametric data, such as a visual analogue pain scale.

Mann Whitney U test
Mann Whitney U test is incorrect. It is a non-parametric version of an unpaired t-test. It can be used to compare two population means obtained from the same population. It can also be used to test whether two population means are equal or not.

stem: The results of an outcome study for a new drug licensed for the treatment of Type 2 diabetes are released. Over an average follow up period of 32 months, 152 major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) events were noted. A point estimate of RRR for MACE events of 18% in favour of the new treatment versus comparators was noted, with a p value of 0.055. A post hoc analysis showed that the drug reduced progression to insulin therapy by 25%. Which of the following is true?
options: The drug is not proven to reduce CV events
The drug is proven to reduce CV events
The drug is proven to reduce progression to insulin
The drug is unlikely to have a positive effect on CV events
The drug should be withdrawn
explanation:
The drug is not proven to reduce CV events
A p value of 0.05 describes the possibility of observing the result by chance is <1 in 20. In practice, a p value of <0.05 is used to describe statistical significance. As such, the value of 0.055 seen here is non-significant. Whilst commentators entertain the notion of a result being ”nearly significant”, this is incorrect.

The drug is proven to reduce progression to insulin
The drug is proven to reduce progression to insulin is incorrect. The reduction in progression to insulin was noted on post-hoc analysis. In order for this to be significant finding, this would need to have been a pre- specified analysis meaning this relationship would have been stipulated as being examined from before the experiment/treatment phase started. One flaw of post-hoc analysis is that patterns and relationships are established after the experiment phase is over. There is a notion that this leads to data-fishing, effectively looking for or choosing data that supports the statement you want to put forward.

stem: In a group of females the heights are normally distributed. 1 in 40 of the females is shorter than 150 cm and 1 in 40 is taller than 170 cm. Which one of the following statements best describes the statistics which describe their heights?
options: Mean height = 150 cm, median = 170 cm, standard deviation = 10 cm
Mean height = 160 cm, median = 160 cm, standard deviation = 10 cm
Mean height = 150 cm, median = 150 cm, standard deviation = 5 cm
Mean height =170 cm, median = 160 cm, standard deviation = 1 cm
Mean height =160 cm, median = 160 cm, standard deviation = 5 cm
explanation:
Mean height =160 cm, median = 160 cm, standard deviation = 5 cm
In a normal distribution: Around 68% of values lie within ± 1 SD of the mean. Around 95% of the values lie within ± 2 SD of the mean.(i.e. 2.5% lie in each tail of the bell curve). Around 95% of the values lie within ± 2 SD of the mean 1 in 40 females = 2.5% of the population, so these are the two tails of the normal distribution. Therefore, 95% of the population lies between 150 and 170. This 95% of the population represents 4 SDs (the mean ± 2SDs). So, the SD will be the range (20) divided by 4, which is 5. Note the data are symmetrical since the distribution is normal. This leaves us with the remaining options of mean height = 150 cm, median = 150 cm, standard deviation = 5 cm and mean height =160 cm, median = 160 cm, standard deviation = 5 cm. The mean and median are both equal in these options which would be the case in a normal distribution, so this isn’t helping us narrow it down.

stem: Which one of the following is a characteristic of sampling?
options: A sample statistic is a point estimate of a population parameter
For a set of observations, the standard deviation is always less than the standard error of the mean
No criteria for sample selection are involved in random sampling
Sampling error arises when we transcribe data incorrectly
The inferential process involves drawing conclusions about the sample
explanation:
A sample statistic is a point estimate of a population parameter
Characteristics of a given sample such as its mean and median are known as sample statistics. Characteristics of a population are known as parameters of population. The sample statistics try to give a point estimate and are not absolute of a population parameter meaning this statement is true.

For a set of observations, the standard deviation is always less than the standard error of the mean
For a set of observations, the standard deviation is always less than the standard error of the mean is incorrect. The standard deviation is used to quantify scatter/variability whereas the standard error of the mean looks at the precision of the mean. The standard error of the mean is the standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size, hence it must always be smaller than the standard deviation. In fact, theChat larger the with AI sample Tutor the smaller the standard error of the mean is compared to the standard deviation.

No criteria for sample selection are involved in random sampling
No criteria for sample selection are involved in random sampling is incorrect. For a random sampling to take place all subjects within the population must have an equal and independent chance of being selected. This means there is a defined criteria in an attempt to prevent bias being introduced.

stem: A group of patients have their albumin levels measured at hospital admission and again 3 weeks into their hospital stay. Which one of the following statistical tests is most appropriate to test the hypothesis that the albumin levels have changed?
options: Chi-squared test
Independent samples t-test
Linear regression
One-way analysis of variance
Paired samples t-test
explanation:
Paired samples t-test
In this study, we are looking at repeat measures in the same individuals, i.e. the samples are paired or dependent. Therefore, the best answer here is to use a paired samples t-test comparing albumin levels before and after a 3-week hospital stay.

Chi-squared test
Chi-squared test is incorrect. A chi-squared test would be looking at frequencies of categorical variables, but albumin is continuous.

Linear regression
Linear regression is incorrect. Linear regression would show a relationship between pre- and post-admission albumin levels, but it would not demonstrate a difference in levels.

stem: In a trial of a new cancer drug, the mortality in the control arm was 12.5% and the relative risk of death for patients receiving the new treatment was 0.8. How many patients must be treated with the new drug to save one life?
explanation:
40
In a clinical trial, the number needed to treat (NNT) is the average number of patients who need to be treated to prevent one additional adverse outcome. NNT = 1 / Absolute risk reduction (ARR) ARR = Control event rate – Experimental event rate The mortality in the experimental arm can be calculated by multiplying the mortality in the control arm by the relative risk: Mortality in experimental arm = 12.5% x 0.8 = 10% ARR = 12.5 – 10 = 2.5% NNT = 1 / 0.025 = 40

stem: An unpaired t-test is used to compare the mean height in two populations. A random sample is taken from each population and the difference in sample means is 10 cm, with a 95% confidence interval from –2 cm to 22 cm. If the true means in the two populations are 150 cm and 165 cm, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: A paired t-test should have been used
A type-1 error has occurred
A type-2 error has occurred
The test shows we can be 95% sure there is a difference
There is no difference in height between the two populations
explanation:
A type-2 error has occurred
Error is a false or mistaken result obtained in a study or experiment. Several kinds of error can occur in epidemiology, for example, due to bias. Random error is the portion of variation in a measurement that has no apparent connection to any other measurement or variable, generally regarded as due to chance. Systematic error often has a recognisable source (e.g. a faulty measuring instrument) and is consistently wrong in a particular direction. A type-1 error is the error of rejecting a true null hypothesis, that is, declaring that a difference exists when it does not. A type -2 error is the error of failing to reject a false null hypothesis, that is, declaring that a difference does not exist when in fact, it does. If a confidence interval crosses 0, it is saying that there is no difference between populations. However, the question tells us that there is a difference between the two groups’ means, so the test result shows that there is not a difference, although there is in reality. Therefore, a type 2 error has occurred.

stem: In an audit of hospital episode statistics, length of hospital stay for acute medical admissions is found to be highly positively skewed with a median of 4 days and an interquartile range of 2–10 days. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: 25% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days
50% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days
90% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days
95% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days
All patients stayed between 2 and 10 days
explanation:
50% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days
Remember: the median is the “middle” value in a sample population. The interquartile range represents ±25% of the population either side of the median. Therefore, 50% of patients stayed between the lengths of stay of the interquartile range.

25% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days
25% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days is incorrect. The interquartile range encompasses two quartiles (50% of the study population), not one quartile (25%).

95% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days
95% of patients stayed between 2 and 10 days is incorrect. The interquartile range encompasses 50% of the study population, not 95%.

stem: What is the type-1 error most closely related to?
options: Correlation coefficient
Positive predictive value
Standard deviation
Standard error of the mean
The p value
explanation:
The p value
A type-1 error occurs when the null hypothesis is falsely rejected leading to a significant difference being observed between two drugs despite there being none. The type-1 error is looking at the significance of a result. The p value is defined as the probability of obtaining a result equal to or more extreme than what was observed when the null hypothesis is true. A p value of 0.05 indicates there is a probability of 5/100 (1 in 20) that the result may have occurred by chance. Again, the p value is looking at the significance of the observed results.

Correlation coefficient
Correlation coefficient is incorrect. The correlation coefficient measures the strength and direction of AI theTutor relationship between two variables. It is a linear relationship and can be either a positive or negative relationship. It does not refer to the significance of the results observed hence it is not closely-related to a type-

Standard deviation
Standard deviation is incorrect. The standard deviation is derived from the square root of the variance and is a measure of the spread of the sample distribution. It measures spread of the results rather than looking at the significance of the results.

stem: You are reviewing adverse event reports associated with medications for the treatment of diabetes. One is a case report on fulminant hepatitis in a patient prescribed a medication for glucose lowering which was launched some 2 years earlier. Blood tests detailed on the yellow card report suggest a rise in alanine transaminase activity to over 3000 U/L and a bilirubin rise to over 150 µmol/l. Ultrasound scan revealed no evidence of hepatic obstruction. On further examination of the adverse event database it appears that 15 similar cases have occurred over the past 2 years, on a background of 800 000 patient years of exposure. Which of the following is the most appropriate next course of action?
options: Change the Marketing Authorisation to confirm that it causes liver failure
Immediately remove the drug from the market
Launch a nested case control study
Launch a prospective cohort study
Perform a study in an appropriate animal model
explanation:
Launch a nested case control study
Given that there have been 16 cases of liver failure, it is crucial to ensure they are properly investigated. A nested case control study examines the medical history of patients that have developed liver failure and compares this to controls that have not, to develop knowledge about potential risk factors. Depending on the results of the study, the Marketing Authorisation may be appropriately revised.

Change the Marketing Authorisation to confirm that it causes liver failure
Change the Marketing Authorisation to confirm that it causes liver failure is incorrect. Immediately changing the Marketing Authorisation runs the risk of changing prescribing information without providing appropriate context to prescribers.

stem: You are examining whether a new treatment for COPD reduces admission rates to the ITU. Published data versus placebo added to standard of care shows a numerical difference in ITU admission rates but this is not statistically significant. Published data for the leading traditional treatment also exists. What is the best way to decide quickly whether the new treatment is more effective than the traditional one?
options: Adjusted indirect comparison using a random effects model
Audit of ITU admissions
Meta-analysis of studies for the novel agent
Prospective head to head clinical study
Qualitative survey
explanation:
Adjusted indirect comparison using a random effects model
The ideal way to test whether the new treatment is more effective than the traditional one would be to perform a prospective randomised controlled trial (RCT). However, this is not one of the options and is also extremely time-consuming and would not provide the quick answer the question is asking for. The random effects model will provide some estimate of comparative effectiveness of the new versus existing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) treatments.

Meta-analysis of studies for the novel agent
Meta-analysis of studies for the novel agent is incorrect. A meta-analysis involves looking and analyzing existing published trials. A meta-analysis could facilitate a quick analysis however, the data would be for the novel agent against a placebo or against the standard of care and not against the placebo and standard of care. Also, the researcher is dependent on previous trials looking at the question being asked in this situation i.e. the previous trials also needed to have looked at ITU admission rates in those taking the novel agent vs those subjects taking the placebo added to standard of care.

stem: You are asked to review the results of a randomised controlled trial of a new agent for treating left ventricular failure. It has completed its final phase III trial with cardiovascular outcomes in over 6 000 individuals. There are several analyses that the company has presented. Which of the following is the most important analysis of efficacy?
options: Completer
Data censored at 90 days
Intention to treat (ITT)
Per protocol
Responder
explanation:
Intention to treat (ITT)
ITT is the preferred primary analysis because it includes all the data from the point of randomisation into the trial. Therefore, this accounts for early dropouts due to lack of efficacy or safety and tolerability events. For this reason, when new drugs are registered, the regulatory agencies count the ITT analysis as the most important analysis of efficacy.

Data censored at 90 days
Data censored at 90 days may give a false view of long-term efficacy because it cannot exclude tolerance/drug effects wearing off after a few weeks of treatment. In trials for indications, such as heart failure, it may include as an extra endpoint to give information about more acute effects which reduce the risks of bounce back into the hospital after first discharge.

stem: How would you best describe the statistical benefit of increasing the sample size of a study comparing metformin with rosiglitazone?
options: A larger sample size decreases the probability of a type-1 error
A larger sample size ensures that the sample must be representative of the population
A larger sample size produces more precise estimates
A larger sample size removes the need for randomisation
A larger sample size will increase the magnitude of the difference between the two treatments
explanation:
A larger sample size produces more precise estimates
The probability of a type-1 error (rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true) is the significance level, which is fixed in advance (often at 5%). Increasing the sample size reduces the standard error, meaning the estimate is more precise and the probability of a type-2 error (not rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false) is reduced.

A larger sample size decreases the probability of a type-1 error
A larger sample size decreases the probability of a type-1 error is incorrect. Because the probability of a type 1 error is fixed in advance, increasing the sample size will not decrease its probability.

A larger sample size removes the need for randomisation
A larger sample size removes the need for randomisation is incorrect. Randomisation is still necessary with large sample sizes because the sample size does not affect biases such selection bias.

stem: A randomised controlled trial recruits 300 patients to receive either standard treatment or a new compound. The main outcome is a measure of disease severity rated on a scale of 0 (poor) to 10 (very good/normal).The average score in the group receiving the new compound is 8.2 compared with 4.5 for those on the standard treatment (p=0.023). Which one of the following should be concluded?
options: A larger study needs to be undertaken
The new compound is significantly better on measures of disease severity than the standard
The new compound is significantly worse than the standard treatment
The severity rating scale is a valid measure of the extent of the disease
The severity rating scale is not sensitive
explanation:
The new compound is significantly better on measures of disease severity than the standard
treatment The trial showed that those receiving the new compound had a higher average score (8.2) compared to those that had the standard treatment (4.5). The p-value here is key. P-values are felt to be statistically significant if the p<0.05. In this case it is 0.023 meaning that this result is statistically significant.

The new compound is significantly worse than the standard treatment
The new compound is significantly worse than the standard treatment is incorrect. For this to be true, the mean score for the standard treatment would need to be greater than the mean score for the new compound. This statement is in fact the opposite of what the trial observed.

stem: A drug company trials a new drug for lowering lipid levels. Patients are randomized into 2 groups, one receiving the drug and the other placebo. The groups are compared at the beginning and end of the trial. What is the best statistical test for comparing mean cholesterols between the two groups?
options: Chi squared test
Logistic regression test
Mann Whitney U test
Paired T test
Unpaired T test
explanation:
Unpaired T test
This tests the null hypothesis that the population means related to two independent, random samples from an approximately normal distribution are equal. In this situation, our subjects have been randomised into two groups and have received different medication so they are independent samples.

Chi squared test
The Chi-squared test in incorrect. This is used for absolute events, ie yes/no classification which is not suitable in this setting.

Logistic regression test

stem: You are approached about evaluating a new test for pancreatic carcinoma. Diagnosis has been confirmed using a combination of CT imaging, ERCP with cytology and histology post tumour resection. 85%

stem: In study comparing incidence rates of malignant melanoma between a sample from Australia and a sample from Norway, how is the power of a statistical test employed to study differences between samples best defined?
options: The probability of not rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false
The probability of not rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true
The probability of obtaining a statistically significant result
The probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false
The probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true
explanation:
The probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false
Statistical significance tests (or hypothesis tests) use sample data to calculate how likely a specified null hypothesis is to be correct. The null hypothesis is usually that there is no difference between groups. The likelihood that the null hypothesis is correct is given as a probability (p) value. The power of a study is the probability (usually expressed as a percentage) of correctly rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false. A significant p-value (<0.05) may lead to rejection of the null hypothesis when is it actually true – this is known as a type I error. Similarly, the p-value may be non-significant (≥0.05) when the null hypothesis is false – this is known as a type II error.

The probability of not rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false
The probability of not rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false is incorrect. The probability of not rejecting the null hypothesis when it is false describes a type II error.
