The relative risk of recurrence for the experimental group compared with the control group was 0.9 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.7–1.1. How should these results be interpreted?
options: Recurrence rates with the new drug were consistent (with 95% confidence) with anywhere between
Recurrence was significantly higher (at the 5% level) in patients receiving the new drug compared
Recurrence was significantly lower (at the 5% level) in patients receiving the new drug compared
The difference between the treatments was too small to be of any clinical importance
There was no difference between the treatments
explanation:
Recurrence rates with the new drug were consistent (with 95% confidence) with anywhere between
a 30% decrease and a 10% increase compared with the standard treatment The relative risk is a common measure of association derived from epidemiological studies of causation, such as cohort and case-control studies. The relative risk expresses how many more times a disease of interest occurs in the group exposed to a particular risk factor compared to the group that is not. In a cohort study, the relative risk is calculated from the ratio of incidence rates in the exposed group and the non-exposed group: Relative risk = Incidence of the disease in the exposed group ÷ Incidence of the disease in the non-exposed group As such, because the relative risk is a ratio, the value is always positive. If there is no association, relative risk = 1 (unity).

stem: You are asked to design a trial for a new antihypertensive agent after taking part in the phase 2 studies. You suspect that it has a power to achieve a relative risk reduction of 18% in CV events. You are examining methodology and statistical tests to determine effectiveness of this agent. What is the power of a statistical test?
options: The probability that it will correctly lead to rejection of a false null hypothesis
The probability that it will falsely lead to rejection of a true null hypothesis
The probability that it will falsely lead to rejection of a false null hypothesis
The probability that it will correctly lead to rejection of a true null hypothesis
The sample size needed to detect a significant difference
explanation:
The probability that it will correctly lead to rejection of a false null hypothesis
This is the definition of the power of a statistical test.

The probability that it will falsely lead to rejection of a true null hypothesis
The probability that it will correctly lead to rejection of a true null hypothesis is incorrect. We do not want to reject a correct null hypothesis. In fact, we want to reject a false null hypothesis.

The probability that it will falsely lead to rejection of a false null hypothesis
The probability that it will falsely lead to rejection of a false null hypothesis is incorrect. This is the opposite of the power of a statistical test where we correctly reject the false null hypothesis.

stem: An oncologist has gained the impression that many women diagnosed as having breast cancer also have high levels of work-related stress. What type of design would be the most practical to test this possible association?
options: Cross-over, randomised cross-over trial
Group comparative, randomised controlled trial
Prospective cohort study
Prospective observational study
Retrospective case-control study
explanation:
Retrospective case-control study
A case-control study is an observational study comparing people with a particular disease (or outcome variable) with a group of people with similar attributes, but without the disease. The past history of exposure to a particular risk factor is compared between cases and controls in order to understand the relationship between different study attributes and the disease of interest. The benefit of a case-control study is that it can be used in relatively rare diseases – each “case” can be compared to an age- and sex-matched “control,” without recruiting the large numbers required for an observational study. If we read the question carefully, it asks us which trial design would be the most practical. This is the best option, because we can use medical records of patients who have been diagnosed with breast cancer and compare them to controls who are age- and sex-matched. A case-control design is practical because it does not require recruitment of large numbers of patients in order to have enough cases of breast cancer (a relatively rare condition). Exposure to the risk factor (work-related stress) can then be compared between the case and control groups.

stem: Anaesthetic recovery time was recorded for 100 consecutive patients undergoing the same surgical procedure. Mean and median times for the procedure were 40 and 65 minutes respectively; the standard deviation was 50 and the range 95 (20 to115 minutes). What is the best way of summarising these data for a paper to a medical journal?
options: Mean = 40; standard deviation = 50
Mean = 40; standard error = 5
Mean = 40; range = 20 to 115
Median = 65; standard deviation = 50
Median = 65; range = 20 to 115
explanation:

This sample population is obviously very skewed, as the mean and median times are so disparate. In addition to this, the mean and median are concentrated towards the lower end of the range, which is wide at 20-115. Therefore, the best way to summarise this skewed data is to use the median and the range, as this is a better way to demonstrate an average and the variance in such an asymmetrical population.

Mean = 40; standard deviation = 50

Median = 65; standard deviation = 50

stem: What does the p-value refer to when considering conventional trial statistics?
options: A value that is always less than 0.05
The probability of having incorrectly rejected the null hypothesis
The probability that the result of the study was obtained by chance
The probability that the alternative hypothesis is true
The probability that the null hypothesis is true
explanation:
The probability that the result of the study was obtained by chance
The p-value is calculated to determine the significance of results in hypothesis testing. The p value is a number between 0 and 1. The null hypothesis is the hypothesis that there is no significant difference between the two arms of the study and any differences observed are due to experimental and sampling errors. The alternative hypothesis accepts that there is observed difference is due to a non-random cause. A large p-value >0.05 indicates weak evidence against the null hypothesis (the null hypothesis has not been rejected). A small p value equal to or less than 0.05 indicates strong evidence against the null hypothesis (the null hypothesis is rejected). This indicates that it is less likely that the relationship between the two groups measured is down to chance. Therefore, the smaller the P value the larger the significance.

A value that is always less than 0.05
A value that is always less than 0.05 is incorrect. The p-value can be greater than 0.05. When the p-value is very small (<0.05) this provides strong evidence against the null hypothesis meaning there is very little chance that the relationship between two groups is purely down to chance. When the p-value is larger this provides weak evidence against the null hypothesis meaning the null hypothesis is accepted.

stem: You are reviewing the results of a study into a new approach to angioplasty versus surgical treatment of angina. Which of the following analyses is most useful when comparing different therapies?
options: Completer analysis
Intention to treat analysis
Per-protocol analysis
Screened and randomised analysis
Sensitivity analysis
explanation:
Intention to treat analysis
Intention to treat analysis involves looking at all people taking part based on the group they were allocated to within a trial regardless of whether or not they actually took the proposed treatment or switched to an alternative or even dropped out. Intention to treat analyses are often used to assess clinical effectiveness as they actually mirror actual clinical practice meaning this is extremely useful data and is a robust way of assessing the effectiveness of a therapy.

Per-protocol analysis
Per-protocol analysis is incorrect. This form of analysis is restricted to the participants who fulfil the protocol in terms of eligibility, interventions and outcome assessment. It only includes subjects who strictly adhered to the treatment guidelines. This is to try and determine the biological effect of the treatments. However, by limiting subject participation will introduce a significant bias.

stem: A prospective population-based case-control study was carried out to assess the relationship between cervical cancer and exposure to human papillomavirus (HPV) and the possible interactions between them. Which evidence level does this trial provide?
options: Evidence level Ia
Evidence level Ib
Evidence level IIb
Evidence level IIc

explanation:

stem: In a review of the use of inhaled corticosteroids for the treatment of acute asthma, the published results of a number of randomised controlled trials were combined to produce a single estimate of the odds ratio for an outcome of hospital admission. Which technique is being described here?
options: Cohort analysis
Cost-effectiveness analysis
Life-table analysis
Meta-analysis
Survival analysis
explanation:
Meta-analysis
The term ‘meta-analysis’ refers to the technique of combining the results of multiple studies (usually randomised controlled trials) to produce one single estimate of treatment effect. By combining many studies, greater precision in this estimate can be achieved than from any one study alone.

Cohort analysis
Cohort analysis is incorrect. It relates to following a group of patients (a cohort) over time e.g. the Framingham heart study.

Life-table analysis is incorrect. It is a technique in which patients are followed up until an event occurs (usually death), and the chance of surviving to any given point in time is estimated e.g. following up patients treated for colorectal cancer.

stem: Cholesterol is measured in populations from Britain, Finland, Japan and the USA, and the four groups are compared using a one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA). Which one of the following graphical methods could best be used to illustrate the results?
options: Bar graph showing the mean cholesterol level of each group
Box plot showing the median, quartiles and range for each group
Four histograms showing the distribution of cholesterol within each group
Plot of the mean cholesterol level with a 95% confidence interval for each group
Scatter plot of cholesterol level against group
explanation:
Plot of the mean cholesterol level with a 95% confidence interval for each group
ANOVA compares means between multiple groups, so displaying the means is the best way to illustrate the results. The means should be presented with confidence intervals to give the reader an idea of whether the differences between the groups were significant. This is therefore the best answer here.

Bar graph showing the mean cholesterol level of each group
Bar graph showing the mean cholesterol level of each group is incorrect. A bar graph would show frequencies of the particular variable of interest, but are not the best method to demonstrate means across populations.

Four histograms showing the distribution of cholesterol within each group
Four histograms showing the distribution of cholesterol within each group is incorrect. Histograms show the distribution of a continuous variable, but without representing the outcomes of ANOVA analysis correctly.

stem: A study examines the relationship between blood pressure and age using linear regression. The result is reported as the equation: Y = 81.3 + 1.3X; where Y is systolic blood pressure in mmHg and X is age in years. How would you best describe the interpretation of the ‘regression coefficient’ of 1.3?
options: A 95% confidence interval for the mean systolic blood pressure in this population is 81.3 ± 1.3
On average, age increased by 1.3 years for every additional 1-mmHg increase in systolic blood
On average, systolic blood pressure increased by 1.3 mmHg for every additional year of age
The average systolic blood pressure measurement must be multiplied by 1.3 for every additional
The range of systolic blood pressures observed in this population was 81.3 ± 1.3 mmHg
explanation:
On average, systolic blood pressure increased by 1.3 mmHg for every additional year of age
The regression equation allows us to predict a Y-value based on an X-value. The intercept tells us the predicted Y-value at 0, but this might not be a reliable prediction as it is likely to be below the range included in the study. The coefficient (the number directly preceding the X-value) tells us how much, on average, the Y-value increases for each additional X-value. In this case, the systolic blood pressure increases by an average of 1.3mmHg for each additional year of age, making this the correct answer.

stem: You are reviewing the results of a clinical trial for a new agent for reducing blood glucose in patients with type 2 diabetes. The data is presented as an intention to treat analysis. What is the definition of an intention to treat (ITT) analysis?

All patients who were intended to receive a treatment but didn’t, are included as part of the placebo
explanation:

This can be quite a complex area; however, the single most important thing to remember is all subjects involved in the study are analysed regardless of the length of their involvement.

All patients who completed the study are included

stem: A new glucose test is developed to detect diabetes. The test has sensitivity 80% and specificity 90%. The positive likelihood ratio is therefore 80/ (100 – 90) = 8. One person in every 17 of those presenting to your clinic has diabetes (i.e. pretest odds = 1/16). For a person who enters your clinic and then tests positive on the new screening test, their post-test odds of having diabetes are which one of the following?
explanation:
50%
Post-test odds = pre-test odds × positive likelihood ratio = (1/16) × 8 = ½ or 50%

6.25%
Post-test odds of 6.25% is incorrect. This describes the pre-test odds (1/16=6.25%).

80%
Post-test odds of 80% is incorrect. This may be referring to the sensitivity. Although the sensitivity is the ability of a test to correctly identify those with the disease, this question is asking for more than this. Here we wish to know the likelihood of a person testing positive and actually having the disease.

stem: In a study of hypertension, systolic blood pressure measurements are found to be approximately normally distributed with a mean 150 mmHg and variance 100. Which one of the following is the single best interpretation of the results?
options: Approximately 95% of measurements in this population lie between 130 and 170 mmHg
Half of the patients had a systolic blood pressure below 100 mmHg
The difference between the highest and lowest measurements was 100 mmHg
The distribution of blood pressure measurements is skewed
We can be 95% confident that the mean of the population lies between 148 and 152 mmHg
explanation:
Approximately 95% of measurements in this population lie between 130 and 170 mmHg
The standard deviation (SD) is a measure of the spread of values in a particular population that is being studied. The smaller the standard deviation, the more closely-grouped the values. Remember: the mean is the arithmetic average of a population i.e. the sum of all values of a variable in a population, divided by the number of subjects in that population. The SD is the square-root of the variance. In a normal distribution: Around 68% of values lie within ± 1 SD of the mean. Around 95% of the values lie within ± 2 SD of the mean. Exactly 95% of the values lie within ± 1.96 SD of the mean (i.e. 2.5% lie in each tail of the bell curve). In this particular question, the SD = 10 (the square-root of the variance, 100). Therefore, as we know that 95% of values lie within ± 2 SDs of the mean, this would give us a range of 130-170 mmHg.

stem: A trial was conducted to look for coagulation abnormalities in patients with tuberculosis. Serum fibrinogen levels were taken as a criterion to diagnose coagulation abnormalities. The subjects were divided into three groups – those without tuberculosis, those with pulmonary tuberculosis and those with disseminated fulminant tuberculosis. The mean fibrinogen level was calculated for each group of patients and compared for significant difference between the groups. Which one of the following tests would be ideal for this measurement?
options: ANOVA
Chi-square test
Pearson test
Regression analysis
Student’s test
explanation:
ANOVA
The analysis of variance (ANOVA) is used when you want to compare two or more means. In this case, we have three means we wish to compare, those without TB, those with primary TB and those with disseminated fulminant TB.

Chi-square test
Chi-square test is incorrect. The Chi-square test is used for nominal data to find out if there is a significant difference between the proportion of observations falling in each group (2 or more) – for example, comparing the proportion of children developing measles between a group receiving a new measles vaccine and a group not given the vaccine

stem: In the first year of a randomised controlled trial to compare two drugs (A and B) for the secondary prevention of myocardial infarction, there were five deaths in 100 patients treated with drug A and ten deaths in 100 patients treated with drug B. The results are reported as X 2 = 1.15, P = 0.28. Which one of the following statements is most appropriate?
options: A larger trial would definitely have given statistically significant results
The null hypothesis of equal drug effects has not been disproved
The two drugs may be considered equivalent
There is a 72% probability that the null hypothesis of equal drug effects is true
There is a 28% probability that the death rate with drug A is lower at one year than the death rate
explanation:
The null hypothesis of equal drug effects has not been disproved
A significance test used data from a sample to show the likelihood that a hypothesis about a population is true. This is provided by the probability or 'p-value'. If p < 0.05 for a set of data, there is less than 5% chance (0.05 = 5%) that the data was obtained by random error or chance. The p value in this case signifies a 28% chance of incorrectly rejecting the possibility that the observed relationship (e.g. between variables) or a difference (e.g. between means) in a sample occurred by pure chance (i.e. the hypothesis that there is no difference between the 2 groups, drug A and drug B). Therefore, the null hypothesis of equal drug effects has not been disproved.

There is a 72% probability that the null hypothesis of equal drug effects is true
There is a 72% probability that the null hypothesis of equal drug effects is true is incorrect. With the p-value calculated at 0.28 this tells you that there is less than a 28% chance that the null hypothesis (I.e.with Chat no difference between the 2 groups, drug A and drug B) is correct. Therefore, rendering the answer of 72% incorrect.

stem: A study of hospital admissions reports a product moment correlation coefficient between age and length of hospital stay of R = 0.76 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.67–0.85. How should these results be interpreted?
options: Inadequate provision of nursing homes prevents the discharge of older patients
Older age was significantly associated with a longer length of stay
Older patients are sicker and require longer stays in hospital
Older patients die more quickly leading to shorter hospital stays
There was no significant relationship between age and length of stay
explanation:
Older age was significantly associated with a longer length of stay
A correlation coefficient indicates whether there is a relationship between two continuous variables. When interpreting a correlation coefficient, one must consider first whether it is a positive or negative number, and also its p-value. If it is positive, then as one variable increases, so does the other. If it is negative, then as one variable increases, the other decreases. This correlation is significant if the p-value is <0.05 (i.e. 5%). It is also significant if the 95% confidence intervals do not cross zero. The question gives us a positive correlation coefficient, which demonstrates that as age increases, so too does the length of stay. The confidence intervals do not cross zero, so the relationship is significant.

There was no significant relationship between age and length of stay
There was no significant relationship between age and length of stay is incorrect. We know that the relationship is significant as the confidence intervals do not cross zero.
